purpose: Every point below is an observable fact about the author's own file as it was served, recorded verbatim with its native line so a later reader is not surprised by it and does not silently 'fix' it. None of these was repaired, completed, reinterpreted or used as a reason to withhold the material. Authors carry mathematical correctness; this file records, it does not adjudicate.

items.verbatim: Now, we acquire the the Auslander--Buchsbaum formula (\cf \cite[Th.\,3.7]{AB57}) for general local rings.
items.observation: 'the the' before 'Auslander--Buchsbaum'. Printed as 'the the' on printed 243.
an extra closing parenthesis after $\cP_{X_j}$; the displayed isomorphism has three terms and only two opening parentheses. Printed as displayed on printed 218.

items.verbatim: {Its proof closely mirrors that of \Cref{purity for rel. dim 1} (also refer to \cite[Th.\,2.8]{GL23}, or can be straightforwardly deduced from~it.}
items.observation: the brace opened before 'Its' is never closed, the parenthesis opened before 'also refer' is never closed, and 'it' has no antecedent inside the parenthetical. Printed on printed 223 with the sentence reading '... mirrors that of Theorem 6.3 (also refer to [GL23, Th. 2.8], or can be straightforwardly deduced from it.'.

items.verbatim: In~addition to its generality, this result leads to an alternative proof of \Cref{a lem on linear algebra} concerning the ``matrix of direct sums of modules''.
items.observation: \Cref{a lem on linear algebra} resolves to A.6 (native 2432), a lemma about a matrix H in M_{m×n}(A) over a module supported on {m_A} admitting a left inverse. The phrase 'matrix of direct sums of modules' describes the consequence, not the lemma's hypothesis. Label resolves; the description is the author's.

items.verbatim: \item The reference for this is \cite[Prop.\,2.4]{Que71}. Assuming the topological Noetherianness of $\Spec A$, this also follows from (i) and the more general \Cref{rf-s2} (or \Cref{normal-s2}).
items.observation: a bare \cite for the primary reference followed by \Cref for the paper-internal alternatives, inside a proof whose other items use \cite[...]{...}. Resolves in print; recorded, not normalised.
the label of the definition of torsors reads 'def of torsos'. It is the target of \Cref at 407 and resolves anyway; recorded, not repaired.

items.kind: heading and statement on one source line
items.observation: the subsection heading and Lemma 3.2 begin on the same line, so no line of the file contains the heading alone. Printed 205 shows the heading followed immediately by the lemma.

items.kind: heading with inline math that the render hyphenates
items.observation: the printed form is 'Case 1: r is arbitrary and d_x = 2.' with the math set inline; the same device repeats at 1386. Recorded because the printed heading cannot be recovered from a plain-text title match.
the appendix is a starred section followed by a manual \refstepcounter, which is what makes A.1-A.8 numbered 'A.n' instead of continuing 9.n. The device is the author's; no \appendix is used.

\egi advances the subsection counter by hand before emitting \item, so the unnumbered Examples block still consumes two subsection numbers; the printed device shows 'Examples (2.7)' on printed 198 and the next numbered statement is Lemma 2.9. Recorded, because a naive counter simulation that ignores \egi misnumbers everything after 2.6.

\numberwithin{equation}{subsection} appears only at 1192, so Claims before section 4 are numbered Claim 2.1 on the section-level equation counter and Claims after it are numbered 4.8.5 and A.2.1. The printed forms confirm this; recorded, not regularised.

every numbered statement is bound to the subsection counter, so statements and subsections alternate in one sequence (Lemma 2.2 inside 2.1, then subsection 2.3). This is a deliberate author/publisher convention and explains why the printed subsection numbers skip; it is not a broken cross-reference.

the five tikzcd diagrams open at 496, 514, 1502, 1674 and 1798 and are syntactically balanced in the source; their arrows and labels were read for the descent definitions at 1492-1521 and the fppf local-cohomology proof, and they agree with the rendered pages that carry them (printed 218, 220, 230-231).
